I had 8 pieces of frozen mango and a chai tea.

Earlier I had two slices of pepperoni pizza and a coffee

function.name: log_food
function.description: Logs a food item with a given portion size to track dietary intake. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

food_name.description: The name of the food to log, such as 'apple', 'bread', or 'chicken breast'.

portion_amount.description: The amount of the food item that was consumed, specified in the unit given by portion_unit. This is a float type value.

portion_unit.description: The unit of measure for the portion amount, such as 'cup', 'grams', or 'slice'.

meal_type.description: The type of meal or snack this food item is being logged for.

log_date.description: The date and time when the food was consumed, in ISO 8601 format such as 'YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ'.

message.reasoning: User wants to log foods. They mention earlier consumption: 2 slices of pepperoni pizza and a coffee. Also current consumption: 8 pieces of frozen mango and a chai tea. We need to log each item. For each log_food call, we need to provide food_name, portion_amount, portion_unit, meal_type (optional). We can assume default meal_type is snack if not specified. But we might want to specify meal_type based on context: maybe breakfast? They didn't specify times. We could log them all as snack. Or we could ask clarifying question about meal_type. But user didn't ask for anything else. We should log each item. We need to call log_food for each item. We have 4 items: frozen mango (8 pieces), chai tea (maybe 1 cup?), pepperoni pizza (2 slices), coffee (1 cup). We need to decide portion_unit: for mango pieces: unit "piece". For chai tea: unit "cup". For pepperoni pizza: unit "slice". For coffee: unit "cup". Provide portion_amount accordingly. For log_date, we can leave default null. So we will make 4 calls.
